vb6:1.0: The Section Derived from the Discourses
vb6:1.1: With ignorance as condition there are (volitional) processes, with (volitional) processes as condition: consciousness, with consciousness as condition: mind and bodily form, with mind and bodily form as condition: the six sense spheres, with the six sense spheres as condition: contact, with contact as condition: feeling, with feeling as condition: craving, with craving as condition: attachment, with attachment as condition: continuation, with continuation as condition: birth, with birth as condition: ageing, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) arise,
vb6:1.2: and so there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering.
vb6:2.2: Not knowing suffering, not knowing the origination of suffering, not knowing the cessation of suffering, not knowing the path leading to the cessation of suffering.
vb6:3.1: Herein, what is ‘with ignorance as condition there are (volitional) processes?’
vb6:3.2: (There is) a meritorious (volitional) process, a demeritorious (volitional) process, an imperturbable (volitional) process, a (volitional) process expressed by way of the body, a (volitional) process expressed by way of speech, a (volitional) process expressed by way of the mind.
vb6:4.1: Herein, what is a meritorious (volitional) process?
vb6:4.2: (There are) wholesome intentions in the sense-world sphere, in the form-world sphere, consisting of generosity, consisting of morality, consisting of meditation,
vb6:4.3: this is said to be a meritorious (volitional) process.
vb6:5.1: Herein, what is a demeritorious (volitional) process?
vb6:5.2: (There are) unwholesome intentions in the sense-world sphere,
vb6:5.3: this is said to be a demeritorious (volitional) process.
vb6:6.1: Herein, what is an imperturbable (volitional) process?
vb6:6.2: (There are) wholesome intentions in the formless-world sphere,
vb6:6.3: this is said to be an imperturbable (volitional) process.
vb6:7.1: Herein, what is a (volitional) process expressed by way of the body?
vb6:7.2: (There is) an intention expressed by way of the body, a (volitional) process expressed by way of the body. (There is) an intention expressed by way of speech, a (volitional) process expressed by way of speech. (There is) an intention expressed by way of the mind, a (volitional) process expressed by way of the mind.
vb6:7.3: This is said to be ‘with ignorance as condition there are (volitional) processes.’
vb6:8.1: Herein, what is ‘with (volitional) processes as condition: consciousness?’
vb6:8.2: (There is) eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-consciousness.
vb6:8.3: This is said to be ‘with (volitional) processes as condition: consciousness.’
vb6:9.1: Herein, what is ‘with consciousness as condition: mind and bodily form?’
vb6:9.2: There is mind, there is bodily form.
vb6:9.4: (There is) the feeling constituent, the perception constituent, the (volitional) processes constituent:
vb6:9.7: (There are) the four great entities, and the bodily form attached to the four great entities,
vb6:9.8: this is said to be ‘bodily form.’
vb6:9.9: Thus, this is mind and this is bodily form.
vb6:9.10: This is said to be ‘with consciousness as condition: mind and bodily form.’
vb6:10.1: Herein, what is ‘with mind and bodily form as condition: the six sense spheres?’
vb6:10.2: (There is the) eye sense sphere, ear sense sphere, nose sense sphere, tongue sense sphere, body sense sphere, mind sense sphere.
vb6:10.3: This is said to be ‘with mind and bodily form as condition: the six sense spheres.’
vb6:11.1: Herein, what is ‘with the six sense spheres as condition: contact?’
vb6:11.2: (There is) eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-contact.
vb6:11.3: This is said to be ‘with the six sense spheres as condition: contact.’
vb6:12.1: Herein, what is ‘with contact as condition: feeling?’
vb6:12.2: (There is) feeling arising from eye-contact, feeling arising from ear-contact, feeling arising from nose-contact, feeling arising from tongue-contact, feeling arising from body-contact, feeling arising from mind-contact.
vb6:12.3: This is said to be ‘with contact as condition: feeling.’
vb6:13.1: Herein, what is ‘with feeling as condition: craving?’
vb6:13.2: (There is) craving for forms, craving for sounds, craving for smells, craving for tastes, craving for tangibles, craving for thoughts.
vb6:13.3: This is said to be ‘with feeling as condition: craving.’
vb6:14.1: Herein, what is ‘with craving as condition: attachment?’
vb6:14.2: (There is) attachment to sense pleasures, attachment to views, attachment to virtue and practice, attachment to self-theories.
vb6:14.3: This is said to be ‘with craving as condition: continuation.’
vb6:15.1: Herein, what is ‘with attachment as condition: continuation?’
vb6:15.2: Continuation is two-fold: there is continuation through (intentional) deeds, there is continuation through rebirth.
vb6:15.5: (There is) a meritorious (volitional) process, a demeritorious (volitional) process, an imperturbable (volitional) process.
vb6:15.6: This is said to be ‘continuation through (intentional) deeds.’
vb6:15.7: All (intentional) deeds leading to continuation is continuation from (intentional) deeds.
vb6:16.2: (There is) continuation in the sense-world spheres, continuation in the form-world spheres, continuation in the formless-world spheres, continuation with perception, continuation without perception, continuation with neither-perception-nor-non-perception, continuation with one constituent, continuation with four constituents, continuation with five constituents.
vb6:16.3: This is said to be ‘continuation through rebirth.’ Thus, this is continuation through (intentional) deeds, this is continuation through rebirth.
vb6:16.4: This is said to be ‘with attachment as condition: continuation.’
vb6:17.1: Herein, what is ‘with continuation as condition: birth?’
vb6:17.2: For the various beings in the various classes of beings (there is) birth, being born, appearing, arising, turning up, the manifestation of the constituents (of mind and bodily form), the acquisition of the sense spheres.
vb6:17.3: This is said to be ‘with continuation as condition: birth.’
vb6:18.1: Herein, what is ‘with birth as condition: ageing, death?’
vb6:18.2: There is ageing, there is death.
vb6:18.4: For the various beings in the various classes of beings (there is) broken teeth, greying hair, and wrinkled skin, the dwindling away of the lifespan, the decay of the sense faculties.
vb6:19.2: For the various beings in the various classes of beings there is a fall, a falling away, a breaking up, a disappearance, a dying, a death, a making of time, the break up of the constituents (of mind and bodily form), the throwing off of the body, a cutting off of the life-faculty:
vb6:19.4: Thus, this is ageing and this is death.
vb6:19.5: This is said to be ‘with birth as condition: ageing, death.’
vb6:20.2: To one touched by misfortune regarding relatives, to one touched by misfortune regarding wealth, to one touched by misfortune regarding health, to one touched by misfortune regarding (loss of) morality, to one touched by misfortune regarding his views, for he who has some sort of misfortune or other, who is touched by some sort of painful thing or another, there is grief, grieving, the state of grieving, inner grief, great inner grief, his mind is sorrowful, being pierced with the dart of grief.

vb6:22.2: That which is bodily pain, bodily disagreeableness, pain arising from contact with the body, disagreeable feeling, pain and painful feeling that is born in the body.
vb6:23.2: That which is mental pain, mental disagreeableness, pain arising from contact with the mind, disagreeable feeling, pain and painful feeling that is born in the mind.
vb6:24.2: To one touched by misfortune regarding relatives, to one touched by misfortune regarding wealth, to one touched by misfortune regarding health, to one touched by misfortune regarding (loss of) morality, to one touched by misfortune regarding his views, for he who has some sort of misfortune or other, who is touched by some sort of painful thing or another, there is desponding, despairing, the state of despondency, the state of despair.
vb6:25.1: So there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering, and so there is an association with this whole mass of suffering, a meeting with it, a connection with it, a manifestation of it.
vb6:25.2: This is said to be ‘the origination of this whole mass of suffering’
vb6:26.1: Through grief and so on ignorance occurs, (though) the beginning of this wheel of continuation is unknown, Devoid of a doer or an experiencer, (it is) empty with a twelvefold emptiness.

vb6:381.2: At whatever time, through having done and accumulated unwholesome deeds, a resultant mind-consciousness element has arisen, connected with equanimity, (having) a form object,...pe... or a sound object, or a smell object, or a taste object, or a tangible object, or a thought object,
vb6:381.3: or referring to whatever (thought), at that time with an unwholesome root as condition there is a (volitional) process, with a (volitional) process as condition: consciousness, with consciousness as condition: mind, with mind as condition: the sixth sense sphere, with the sixth sense sphere as condition: contact, with contact as condition: feeling, with feeling as condition: resolve, with resolve as condition: continuation, with continuation as condition: birth, with birth as condition: ageing, death,
vb6:381.4: and so there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering.
vb6:382.1: Herein, what is ‘with an unwholesome root as condition there is a (volitional) process?’
vb6:382.2: That which is volition, intention, intentionality:
vb6:382.3: this is said to be ‘with an unwholesome root as condition there is a (volitional) process.’
vb6:383.1: Herein, what is ‘with a (volitional) process as condition: consciousness?’
vb6:383.2: That which is thought, mind, mentality,...pe... heart, consciousness, mind, the mind sense sphere, the mind faculty, consciousness, the consciousness constituent, the mind-consciousness element arising from that:
vb6:383.3: this is said to be ‘with a (volitional) process as condition: consciousness.’
vb6:384.1: Herein, what is ‘with consciousness as condition: mind?’
vb6:384.2: (There is) the feeling constituent, the perception constituent, the (volitional) processes constituent:
vb6:384.3: this is said to be ‘with consciousness as condition: mind.’
vb6:385.1: Herein, what is ‘with mind as condition: the sixth sense sphere?’
vb6:385.2: That which is thought, mind, mentality,...pe... heart, consciousness, mind, the mind sense sphere, the mind faculty, consciousness, the consciousness constituent, the mind-consciousness element arising from that:
vb6:385.3: this is said to be ‘with mind as condition: the sixth sense sphere.’
vb6:386.1: Herein, what is ‘with the sixth sense sphere as condition: contact?’
vb6:386.2: That which is contact, contacting, close contacting, the state of being in close contact:
vb6:386.3: this is said to be ‘with the sixth sense sphere as condition: contact.’
vb6:387.1: Herein, what is ‘with contact as condition: feeling?’
vb6:387.2: That which is neither mental agreeableness nor disagreeableness, neither painful nor pleasant experience born of contact with the mind, neither painful nor pleasant feeling born of contact with the mind:
vb6:387.3: this is said to be ‘with contact as condition: feeling.’
vb6:388.1: Herein, what is ‘with feeling as condition: resolve?’
vb6:388.2: That which is resolve of the mind, resolution, the state of being resolved on that (mind):
vb6:388.3: this is said to be ‘with feeling as condition: resolve.’
vb6:389.1: Herein, what is ‘with resolve as condition: continuation?’
vb6:389.2: Except for resolve, (it is) the feeling constituent, the perception constituent, the (volitional) processes constituent, the consciousness constituent:
vb6:389.3: this is said to be ‘with resolve as condition: continuation.’
vb6:390.1: Herein, what is ‘with continuation as condition: birth?’
vb6:390.2: That which for various things is birth, being born, return, turning up, manifestation:
vb6:390.3: this is said to be ‘with continuation as condition: birth.’
vb6:391.1: Herein, what is ‘with birth as condition: ageing, death?’
vb6:391.2: There is ageing, there is death.
vb6:391.4: For various things (there is) ageing, agedness, the dwindling away of the lifespan:
vb6:391.7: For various things (there is) destruction, decay, a breaking up, a complete breaking up, impermanence, a disappearance:
vb6:391.9: Thus, this is ageing and this is death,
vb6:391.10: this is said to be ‘with birth as condition: ageing, death.’
vb6:392.1: So there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering,
vb6:392.2: and so there is an association with this whole mass of suffering, a meeting with it, a connection with it, a manifestation of it.
vb6:392.3: This is said to be ‘the origination of this whole mass of suffering.’
